source.title: Active Adaptation, Not Static Defense: Temporal Dynamics of Preventative Steering in Adversarial Fine-Tuning
source.authors: Jing Guan; Ya-Chao Yang; Zhao-Liang Liu; Yu-Yao Zhang; Fan-Yu Meng; Jun-Lan Feng

record.file_problem: The paper text is substantially present. Some figure labels and a portion of the Table 4 area are garbled, but the main text and tabulated results are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper uses harmful fine-tuning vulnerability as motivation and studies a training-time defense against persona drift. Its own results concern Preventative Steering, its optimization dynamics, and PIS—not the claim versions about refusal loss, first-token KL concentration, bypasses, or token-depth safety.
record.gate_note: The study reports harmful-trait scores and safety-benchmark results for its defense experiments, plus parameter-offset preservation experiments. These do not measure refusal/compliance rates after harmful or benign fine-tuning, per-token KL by response position, or bypass success. PIS-versus-static results are the paper's proposed method performance and are not recorded as claim-version rows.
record.test_reason: The paper uses malicious fine-tuning vulnerability only as motivation. It studies Preventative Steering and its PIS schedule as a defense. Its measures are persona-trait expression scores (evil, sycophancy, hallucination) after fine-tuning on data built to induce those traits, plus safety-benchmark averages comparing defense variants. It never reports harmful-request compliance before versus after fine-tuning, per-token KL by position, prefill or suffix bypasses, localization of safety weights, or token-depth deepening.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. Preventative Steering protects through active adaptation during fine-tuning, not through a static weight or activation offset. PIS improves safety averages and lowers trait scores relative to static steering on Qwen2.5-7B, Qwen2.5-32B and Gemma-3-12B.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies Preventative Steering with full-parameter fine-tuning, response-token-only injection at about 70% model depth, and a mixed persona direction; it adds temporal-dynamics, parameter-offset, and PIS experiments. It does not reproduce the harmful/benign fine-tuning refusal-rate measurements or first-token KL method in the claim's cited originals.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with steering strength and timing, injection layer, and model. The paper reports non-monotonic static-strength and PIS upper-bound sweeps and a substantial injection-layer effect.

fits_no_version.finding: Preventative Steering during trait-inducing fine-tuning lowers evil, sycophancy and hallucination expression scores compared with unprotected fine-tuning on Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Response-token Preventative Steering during malicious fine-tuning suppresses trained persona-trait drift.

fits_no_version.finding: Neither preserving the steering-induced parameter offset (IDP) nor reinjecting it as an activation vector maintains protection.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The protection from Preventative Steering depends on ongoing injection, not on a static weight offset.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The paper states that it studies only three undesirable traits and a limited set of model families. The reported trait scores use an automated judge; no uncertainty estimates are stated in the cited tables. The evidence does not directly assess the claim's refusal-rate or token-position measures.
record.rows_left_out: The PIS-versus-static results in Table 4 and the static-strength, layer, and multiplier sweeps in Figures 5–7 and Table 5 were not extracted: these report the paper's proposed defense performance rather than an outcome on a claim version. Mechanistic plots and directional decompositions in Figures 2–4 and Table 8 were also left out because they measure Preventative Steering optimization dynamics, not the claim's token-position safety behavior.

untested.parts: No harmful-request compliance or refusal rate is reported for the aligned model before versus after harmful fine-tuning. Trait scores measure deliberately trained persona traits.
There is no benign fine-tuning experiment.
There is no per-token KL by response position.
There are no prefill, suffix or decoding bypass experiments.
Attention output projections carry steering-induced updates, but no test shows a small set of weights carries safety.
Causes of token-depth shallowness are not studied.
No token-depth deepening training is studied.

missing.what: Under malicious fine-tuning without defense, the safety score is 23.09, versus 85.72 with embedded PIS. No pre-fine-tuning safety score is given, so the size of the drop the attack causes cannot be read.

record.verdict_notes: No verdicts are given because no row measures harmful-request compliance arising from fine-tuning against a pre-fine-tuning baseline. The Table 1 base-model row (0.00/1.30/1.02) versus unprotected fine-tuning (7.38/8.66/9.00) shows deliberately trained persona traits. That is induced behaviour, not a V1 compliance rate.

versions.untested_parts: No harmful-request compliance or refusal rate after fine-tuning is reported; the harmful-trait scores are not a measure of that behavior.
No ordinary or benign fine-tuning experiment is reported.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL analysis is reported.
No compliant-opening prefill, adversarial-suffix, or decoding-change bypass experiment is reported.
The paper examines whether a particular steering-induced parameter offset can preserve protection, but does not identify or test whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
The paper studies the dynamics of Preventative Steering, not whether data or an objective causes first-token safety shallowness.
PIS changes steering intensity over training, but the paper does not train safety to spread beyond early response tokens or test such token-depth robustness.
